title: Blunt-join comparison for a right-anodyne inclusion
statement:
Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, horns, internal functor simplicial sets and quasicategories as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A right anodyne map is in the smallest class containing isomorphisms and all horn inclusions $\Lambda_j^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $m\geq1$, $0<j\leq m$, and closed under pushouts, transfinite composition and retracts. Here a monomorphism is a degreewise injective map. Pushouts are colimits of spans in simplicial sets in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. A transfinite composite is $Z_0\to Z_\theta$ for a diagram indexed by a small ordinal, with $Z_\beta=\varinjlim_{\alpha<\beta}Z_\alpha$ at every nonzero limit $\beta\leq\theta$. A map $f:U\to V$ is a retract of $g:U'\to V'$ if there are maps $a:U\to U'$, $b:V\to V'$, $r:U'\to U$, $s:V'\to V$ satisfying $ga=bf$, $fr=sg$, $ra=1_U$, and $sb=1_V$. For simplicial sets $X,Y$, define their blunt join by the pushout
$$X\diamond Y=X\amalg_{X\times\{0\}\times Y}(X\times\Delta^1\times Y)\amalg_{X\times\{1\}\times Y}Y,$$
where the two attaching maps to $X,Y$ are the coordinate projections. If $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ is right anodyne, the canonical map
$$\theta_i:B\amalg_A(A\diamond\Delta^0)\hookrightarrow B\diamond\Delta^0$$
is a monomorphism and a categorical equivalence. Here categorical equivalence of $u:U\to V$ means that restriction $h\operatorname{Fun}(V,\mathcal C)\to h\operatorname{Fun}(U,\mathcal C)$ is an equivalence of ordinary categories for every quasicategory $\mathcal C$ in any sufficiently large universe; $hS$ is the category generated by the vertices and edges of $S$, with degenerate edges as identities and each $2$-simplex imposing its composition relation. Consequently, for every quasicategory $\mathcal C$ and every simplicial map $f_0:B\amalg_A(A\diamond\Delta^0)\to\mathcal C$, there is a simplicial map $f:B\diamond\Delta^0\to\mathcal C$ satisfying $f\theta_i=f_0$.
